title: Canonical K-flat chain model of the internal open projection
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion, and $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On small representatives of the pro-étale sites in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for $T=U,Z$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ for internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with relative tensor $\otimes_{\Lambda_T}$ [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Let $E=j_!:\mathcal M_U\to\mathcal M_Z$ be the coefficient-linear extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and $R=j^*:\mathcal M_Z\to\mathcal M_U$ the module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star], with their specified adjunction $E\dashv R$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], unit $u$ and counit $v$. Use the actual relative tensor comparison $\nu_{A,B}:RA\otimes_{\Lambda_U}RB\to R(A\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}B)$ of module pullback, induced by its abelian pullback structure and scalar extension along $\alpha_j$: it is the inverse of the ordinary comparison $t_{A,B}$ of [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison] for $f=j$, under that node's identification of its inverse image with $R$.
Let $e=D(E)$ and $r=Lj^*\cong D(R)$ on ordinary unbounded derived categories, with the adjunction obtained by deriving this specified module adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]; write $\eta,\varepsilon$ for its unit and counit. Use the relative K-flat derived tensors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $\mu$ be the actual lax tensorator of $r$, inverse to its actual oplax map induced by module pullback and localization. Write $Q_T$ for localization of complexes of $\mathcal M_T$, and $\theta$ for the underived maps in [lem-pd-open-module-balanced-projection]. Flat means that relative tensor with the module is exact; K-flat means that direct-sum total tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [pur713-def-kflat-module].
For arbitrary unbounded complexes $P$ in $\mathcal M_U$ and $Q$ in $\mathcal M_Z$, the maps $\theta_{P^p,Q^q}$, followed by the coproduct insertions, induce a natural chain isomorphism
$$\Phi_{P,Q}:E\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\Lambda_U}RQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(EP\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}Q).$$
The total terms are direct sums over $p+q=n$ and the differential on that summand is $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$. Its chain inverse has the inverse bidegree maps. Extension $E$ preserves flat modules and K-flat complexes, and $R$ preserves complexes that are K-flat with flat terms.
If $P,Q$ are K-flat with flat terms, put $K=Q_UP$ and $L=Q_ZQ$. Under the canonical termwise exact-functor identifications and the K-flat derived tensor identifications, both the source and target of $Q_Z(\Phi_{P,Q})$ identify respectively with $e(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_U}rL)$ and $eK\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_Z}L$, and there is the equality of morphisms
$$Q_Z(\Phi_{P,Q})=\varepsilon_{eK\otimes L}\circ e(\mu_{eK,L})\circ e(\eta_K\otimes1_{rL}).$$
This equality uses the specified $\eta,\varepsilon,\mu$, with the fixed internal-to-section-module comparisons of [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison]. On bidegree $(p,q)$ its representative is $v_{E(P^p)\otimes Q^q}\circ E(\nu_{E(P^p),Q^q})\circ E(u_{P^p}\otimes1)$, hence exactly the indicated $\theta_{P^p,Q^q}$. No boundedness, finite Tor dimension, or constructibility is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-pd-open-module-balanced-projection], $E,R$ are additive and exact and $u:1\to RE$ is a natural isomorphism. The specified adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that $E$ preserves the degreewise coproducts indexed by $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$. These are small in the chosen module universe. The coproduct comparison used below is the unique one commuting with every insertion. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], termwise $E$ and $R$ preserve acyclic complexes. Termwise $u$ is a chain isomorphism: its chain equation is precisely naturality of $u$ with respect to each differential.

source.place: Derived version; the small-coproduct and exactness inputs to termwise totalization

proof.text:
Using that coproduct comparison, define $\Phi^n$ by $\Phi^n E(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\theta_{P^p,Q^q}$ for $p+q=n$. Naturality in the first and second variables of [lem-pd-open-module-balanced-projection] gives respectively
$$\theta_{P^{p+1},Q^q}E(d_P^p\otimes1)=(E d_P^p\otimes1)\theta_{P^p,Q^q},\qquad
\theta_{P^p,Q^{q+1}}E(1\otimes R d_Q^q)=(1\otimes d_Q^q)\theta_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
Since $E$ is additive, it preserves the scalar $(-1)^p$. Adding the two identities proves the chain equation on each insertion for the differential of [pur713-def-kflat-module], hence on the whole sum. The same equations for $\theta^{-1}$ define a chain inverse. The two composites are identities on every insertion, so are identities. Naturality for any pair of chain maps follows from the same two-variable naturality. This proves the claimed chain isomorphism for arbitrary unbounded $P,Q$.

source.place: Derived version, sentence “Applying the sheaf formulas termwise to the double complexes”; explicit signed sum and inverse

proof.text: If $M$ is flat on $U$, apply exact $R$ to a short exact sequence on $Z$, tensor with $M$, and apply exact $E$. The natural isomorphisms $\theta_{M,-}$ identify the result with tensoring the original sequence with $EM$. Thus $EM$ is flat. If $N$ is flat on $Z$, apply exact $E$ to a short exact sequence on $U$, tensor with $N$, and use $\theta_{-,N}^{-1}$; this is the $E$-image of the sequence tensored with $RN$. Applying exact $R$ and conjugating by $u^{-1}:RE\cong1$ makes that tensor sequence short exact. Thus $R$ preserves flat modules as well. All identifications are natural in the arrows of the sequences, as asserted in [lem-pd-open-module-balanced-projection].

source.place: Derived version, flatness needed for flat-term representatives; explicit short-exact-sequence test

proof.text: Let $P$ be K-flat on $U$ and let $A$ be any acyclic complex on $Z$. Step 1 makes $RA$ acyclic. By the K-flat test of [pur713-def-kflat-module], $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes RA)$ is acyclic; exact $E$ preserves this by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. The isomorphism $\Phi_{P,A}$ of Step 2 identifies its $E$-image with $\operatorname{Tot}(EP\otimes A)$. This is the defining test for $EP$ to be K-flat. There is no restriction on the terms of $P$.

source.place: Derived version, extension by zero and the acyclic tensor test

proof.text:
Let $Q$ be K-flat on $Z$ and $C$ acyclic on $U$. Exact $E$ makes $EC$ acyclic. The signed symmetry sends the $(p,q)$ summand of $EC\otimes Q$ to the $(q,p)$ summand of $Q\otimes EC$ by $(-1)^{pq}$ times the module tensor flip; the two differential components commute with this map because $(-1)^{(p+1)q}=(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^p(-1)^{p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$, and its square is the identity. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(EC\otimes Q)$ is acyclic by K-flatness of $Q$. Applying $R$ to $\Phi_{C,Q}$ of Step 2 and precomposing with $u_{\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes RQ)}$ gives a chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes RQ)\cong R\operatorname{Tot}(EC\otimes Q).$$
The right side is acyclic by exactness. The same signed symmetry converts this into the K-flat test for $RQ$. Step 3 also gives flat terms when $Q$ has flat terms. The flip is the symmetry of relative module tensor [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor], which the exact symmetric monoidal comparison [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] carries to the section-module one; no commutation of $R$ with an infinite sum has been presumed.

source.place: Derived version, open inverse-image K-flatness argument; signed tensor flip written explicitly

proof.text: Now suppose $P,Q$ are K-flat with flat terms. Steps 3–5 imply that $EP,RQ$ (and $REP$) have these same properties. By the relative K-flat model of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], $Q_U\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes RQ)$ represents $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}rL$, and $Q_Z\operatorname{Tot}(EP\otimes Q)$ represents $eK\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$. Here exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supplies the identifications $Q_Z EP\cong eK$ and $Q_U RQ\cong rL$. Applying the same exact factorization to $E\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes RQ)$ identifies its localization with $e(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}rL)$. These are the fixed model comparisons: [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies their internal and section-module versions, preserving flatness, K-flatness and total tensor.

source.place: Derived version, the K-flat model identifications of source and target

proof.text: The cochain adjunction $E\dashv R$ has unit $u_{P^p}$ and counit $v_{Q^q}$ in each degree: its Hom bijection is applied degreewise, and its naturality says exactly that transposes of chain maps are chain maps. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to this adjunction and to the quasi-isomorphism localizations. Both functors descend by exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Its displayed unit and counit formulas identify $\eta$ with $Q(u)$ and $\varepsilon$ with $Q(v)$ under those factors. This is the specified derived adjunction in the statement; [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies precisely these units and counits with the independently specified section-module ones.

source.place: Derived version, localization of the specified adjunction rather than a new choice of adjunction

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Tot}(EP\otimes Q)$ and let $N_{EP,Q}:\operatorname{Tot}(REP\otimes RQ)\to RT$ have bidegree components $\nu_{E(P^p),Q^q}$ and the canonical coproduct comparisons. Its inverse is the total map of $t$ in [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison]; the chain equations are the naturality equations of Step 2 with $R$ in place of $E$. The representative normalization in that definition, restricted to the K-flat pair $EP,Q$, identifies $Q_U(N_{EP,Q})$ with the inverse of its normalized derived oplax comparison. It is the actual $\mu_{eK,L}$: [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies the actual oplax map with the canonical ringed tensor comparison, and identifies its inverse with the actual lax map. The ordinary comparison used here is exactly $t$, whose inverse is the $\nu$ fixed in the item. Thus this step concerns these specified maps, with the exact factors and K-flat tensor comparisons of Step 6.

source.place: Derived version; normalized actual lax tensorator on K-flat representatives

proof.text:
By Steps 6–8, the displayed derived composite is represented by the chain composite
$$E\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes RQ)\xrightarrow{E\operatorname{Tot}(u_P\otimes1)}E\operatorname{Tot}(REP\otimes RQ)\xrightarrow{E(N_{EP,Q})}ERT\xrightarrow{v_T}T.$$
On the insertion indexed by $(p,q)$, naturality of $v$ with respect to $E(P^p)\otimes Q^q\to T^{p+q}$ and the defining coproduct comparisons make this composite
$$\iota'_{p,q}\,v_{E(P^p)\otimes Q^q}\,E(\nu_{E(P^p),Q^q})\,E(u_{P^p}\otimes1)=\iota'_{p,q}\theta_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
The last equality is the formula in [lem-pd-open-module-balanced-projection]. The equality on all insertions proves equality of degree maps and hence chain maps with $\Phi_{P,Q}$ of Step 2. Localization preserves this equality and composition, giving exactly the asserted equality with $\varepsilon\circ e(\mu)\circ e(\eta\otimes1)$ under the fixed comparisons. No finite-sum, boundedness, constructibility or Tor-dimension argument occurs.
